solid_envelopes.source: Native lh/rh.pial and lh/rh.white; vertices and triangles unchanged

surface_shading.meaning: Sulcal-depth morphometry; positive values mark sulci
surface_shading.concavity: _CONCAVITY: normal-projected one-ring displacement / mean edge length; one field-only averaging pass on the intact pial hemisphere
surface_shading.intensity: _T1: trilinear orig.mgz at corresponding pial/white midpoints in tkregister RAS; illustrative brightness, not measured optical albedo

ribbon_labels.source: Native lh/rh.aparc.a2009s.annot, one region index per vertex; a triangle belongs to the parcel holding most of its vertices

surface_shading.meaning: Sulcal-depth morphometry; positive values mark sulci
surface_shading.concavity: _CONCAVITY: normal-projected one-ring displacement / mean edge length; one field-only averaging pass on the intact pial hemisphere
surface_shading.intensity: _T1: trilinear orig.mgz at corresponding pial/white midpoints in tkregister RAS; illustrative brightness, not measured optical albedo

ribbon_labels.source: Native lh/rh.HCPMMP1.annot, one region index per vertex; a triangle belongs to the parcel holding most of its vertices

networks.label: Yeo 7-network cortical organisation
networks.method: Schaefer2018 parcels collapsed to their published Yeo network; carried per vertex, never interpolated
networks.composition: Cortical parcels: shares of assigned source vertices. NextBrain cortical regions: shares of assigned projected cortical voxels. Unassigned samples are excluded; these are not surface-area shares.

cab_np.label: Cole-Anticevic Brain-wide Network Partition (CAB-NP) v1.1.6
cab_np.license: CAB-NP License (Rutgers University and Yale University), non-commercial use only
cab_np.method: Each HCP-MMP1.0 area takes the network CAB-NP assigns it, matched by published area name in each hemisphere; carried per area, never per vertex

functional_regions.label: Functional divisions (Glasser 2016 sections; Glasser 2016, Rolls 2022 and Rolls 2023 named regions)
functional_regions.method: Each HCP-MMP1.0 area takes the section and, where a source names one, the named region whose published area list holds it, matched by area name in each hemisphere; carried per area, never per vertex

neuropsych_domains.label: Neuropsychological domains (Neurosynth consistency maps on HCP-MMP areas and aseg structures)
neuropsych_domains.license: Open Database License (ODbL) 1.0; derived area scores shared under the same licence
neuropsych_domains.method: Each domain's Neurosynth abstract term (version 7, TF-IDF at least 0.001); MKDA chi-square uniformity z with a 6 mm kernel, sampled between fsaverage's white and pial surfaces and averaged per HCP-MMP area, and resampled onto fsaverage's aseg and averaged per grey-matter structure. An area or structure belongs to every domain whose mean z reaches 3, its strength measured against the domain's cortical maximum; in the overview of the eleven assessment domains it takes the one whose z is the largest share of that domain's cortical maximum. Carried per area, never per vertex

neurosynth_terms.label: Neurosynth term search (consistency maps of chosen version 7 abstract terms on HCP-MMP areas and aseg structures)
neurosynth_terms.license: Open Database License (ODbL) 1.0; derived area scores shared under the same licence
neurosynth_terms.method: Neurosynth version 7 abstract terms naming a function, task, stimulus, state, behaviour or clinical population, each derived as the domains are: studies whose abstract uses the term at a TF-IDF of at least 0.001 against every other study, MKDA chi-square uniformity z with a 6 mm kernel, averaged per HCP-MMP area between fsaverage's white and pial surfaces and per aseg grey-matter structure. An area or structure is drawn where its mean z reaches 3. Carried per area, never per vertex

display_geometry.method: Marching cubes, then bounded Taubin smoothing that moves no voxel centre across the surface
Marching cubes, then bounded Taubin smoothing that moves no voxel centre across the surface

detail_levels.label: Learning anatomy
detail_levels.palette_method: Distinct teaching colours for display units, not the source LUT

display_geometry.method: Explicit source-label unions; bounded Taubin display smoothing

boundary_convention: Barycentric vertex cells on mixed-label triangles
limitations: Z-Anatomy reference cord in its anatomical posture; seated below the brainstem by translation alone, not registered to this subject’s MRI. Segment levels and root counts are the reference model’s, not this subject’s.
Its cross-section is Z-Anatomy’s schematic one, swept unchanged along the cord, so every level shows the same arrangement.
Z-Anatomy files this tract under the anterior funiculus, but its surface lies inside the intermediate zone.
One published individual's anatomy, not an averaged template: it is nobody else's brain, and no part of it is clinically validated.
Destrieux labels are this subject's own FreeSurfer parcellation.
HCP-MMP is the published Mills fsaverage projection, resampled again onto this brain through FreeSurfer's registered spheres: two registrations, and native HCP space is neither of them.
Labels projected between brains are bounded by that registration, not by the accuracy of the published parcellation.
The source T1 was defaced before release: facial features were obscured; the brain was not altered.
This FreeSurfer aseg contains no left choroid plexus (31), right choroid plexus (63), optic chiasm (85) labels; those coarse aseg regions are not exported.
Destrieux labels identify gyri and sulci; HCP labels identify multimodal areas.
Subvertex label boundaries are visualization conventions, not measured boundaries.
FreeSurfer's subcortical segmentation uses a 1 mm grid; fine nuclei and cerebellar folia are unresolved in it.

NextBrain labels are this brain's own Bayesian segmentation at 0.4 mm, estimated from a 1 mm T1 with a histological atlas as prior: where neighbouring structures share their T1 contrast, the atlas rather than the scan places the boundary between them.
Learning anatomy is a derived overview of explicit label unions, with display smoothing bounded to 0.6 mm. Measurements remain source-voxel counts; smoothness does not add anatomical resolution.
Learning brainstem territories omit separately displayed nuclei and pathways; they are not complete brainstem subdivisions.
Learning publishes the cerebellar cortex and the deep nuclei, but not cerebellar white matter, which would enclose the nuclei; the nuclei therefore sit in the space it occupies.
Learning cerebellar lobules are FastSurfer CerebNet's segmentation of this brain's 1 mm T1 in SUIT nomenclature; vermis I–V is part of lobules I–IV and V, and folia are not resolved.
Cerebellar lobules are published as teaching surfaces only; MRI cuts carry no lobule labels.
Learning units come from three segmentations of the same brain (aseg, NextBrain and CerebNet), so surfaces from different sources can overlap slightly where they meet.
NextBrain nuclei below the geometry threshold, its white matter, its cerebellar cortical layers and its cortical parcels have no mesh and remain cut labels only.
Only one internal-anatomy detail level is drawn at a time; the coarse and fine layers segment the same anatomy.
Internal solids are marching-cubes surfaces smoothed for display by at most 0.6 mm and never across a voxel centre; between voxel centres their boundaries are a display convention, not a measurement.
Where a segmented structure meets itself at a corner its surface pinches there and is not a two-manifold; validation counts those edges, and the volume each surface encloses stays definite.
NextBrain cortical parcels are published as ctx-rh- names for both hemispheres, an artefact of the reused label block; the hemisphere field is authoritative.
Cortical regions are surface patches; the solids that cap them at a cut are closed by extruding each patch to its corresponding white-surface vertices.
A cut assigns each source triangle to the parcel holding most of its vertices, so a parcel boundary on a cut can differ from the surface's barycentric boundary by one triangle.
Networks describe group resting-state functional connectivity from 1000 subjects, not a region's measured function in this brain.

Cortical parcel network shares count assigned source vertices; NextBrain cortical region shares count assigned projected cortical voxels. Unassigned samples are excluded. Neither is a surface-area fraction.
Networks are a group average projected onto one person's folds through registered spheres; they are not this individual's measured networks.
CAB-NP networks come from group resting-state connectivity of Human Connectome Project participants, not from this brain's measured function, and reach this brain through the same HCP-MMP projection.
CAB-NP assigns each HCP-MMP area whole to one network, so its colour boundaries are HCP-MMP's boundaries. It colours that atlas's areas only.
CAB-NP assigns the hemispheres separately; 13 areas belong to a different network on each side, as published.

Functional divisions are published groupings of HCP-MMP1.0 areas: the 22 sections of Glasser et al. (2016) and named regions from Glasser et al. (2016) and Rolls et al. (2022, 2023). They reach this brain through the HCP-MMP projection and are not measured in it.

A functional division's borders are HCP-MMP's area borders. No border is drawn for a name no source defines as a set of HCP-MMP areas: dorsomedial prefrontal cortex, a dorsolateral prefrontal cortex narrower than Glasser's section, the temporoparietal junction and the intraparietal sulcus have no named region and are shown only within Glasser's sections.

Glasser's supplement places six areas (23c, 52, PFcm, TF, a47r, pOFC) in one section in its Table 1 and in another in its section texts; the sections follow Table 1's primary column, and the alternative is published beside each.

Neuropsychological domains are Neurosynth consistency maps of the published activation literature, averaged over each HCP-MMP area on fsaverage and reaching this brain through its HCP-MMP projection. They show where studies using a domain's term report activation in groups of healthy people, not what this brain does, and not what damage to an area would impair.

Most terms are used by at least 100 studies. Eleven clinically pertinent ones rest on fewer, down to 74 (sustained attention, smell, navigation, verbal fluency, taste, interoception, gestures, object recognition, moral reasoning, arithmetic, speech perception); their maps are weaker evidence, and every function names its study count.

limitations.Consciousness (74 studies) was derived a: its map reached one area, MT, at z 3.1, and no structure.

limitations: Each domain is one abstract term chosen to name the clinical domain, and a study counts when its abstract uses the term, whatever task it ran. Consistency z grows with the number of such studies, so domains backed by large literatures (attention, language, working memory) reach more areas than executive function or social cognition; regions engaged by most demanding tasks, such as the anterior insula and intraparietal sulcus, reach several domains.

Besides the cortex, each map is averaged over FreeSurfer's grey-matter structures (thalamus, caudate, putamen, pallidum, hippocampus, amygdala, accumbens, ventral diencephalon, cerebellar cortex and brainstem), each as a whole on fsaverage's own segmentation. The 6 mm kernel is large beside the smaller nuclei, the few millimetres between MNI305 and MNI152 matter more there, and studies report fewer subcortical coordinates, so these are weaker evidence than the cortical areas. White matter, NextBrain's finer nuclei and the teaching set's units are not scored, and a lesion check on them is reported as not measured.
Neurosynth's MNI152 maps are sampled on fsaverage's surfaces, whose MNI305 space differs from MNI152 by a few millimetres; whole-area averages absorb most, not all, of that difference.

Searched terms are words chosen from Neurosynth's vocabulary for naming a function, task, stimulus, state or behaviour; unlike the curated functions, no map was checked against what it names or against lesion studies. A term's map shows where studies whose abstract uses it report activation, whatever their task.

A population term (schizophrenia, aphasia, smokers) gathers studies of that group, most comparing it with healthy people. Its map shows where those studies report activation, not where damage causes the condition.
Consistency z grows with study count, so a term with few studies reaches fewer areas, and every term names its study count.

Gyral white matter is FreeSurfer's wmparc: each voxel within 5 mm of cortex takes the nearest Desikan cortical label whichever surface atlas is shown, and deeper white matter is unsegmented and belongs to no region.

sources.procedure: scripts/extract_spinal_cord.py: evaluated Blender modifiers, interior sheets dropped, open sweep ends filled
scripts/segment_nextbrain.py: SuperSynth, then NextBrain Bayesian segmentation (segment_fireants.py --mode invivo --device cpu) of each hemisphere at 0.4 mm, joined on one 0.4 mm surface-RAS grid

crop.rule: bounding box of brain.mgz > 0, plus 20 voxels, within the grid

hemisphere_join.method: nearest neighbour from each hemisphere's own grid onto one surface-RAS grid
hemisphere_join.overlap_rule: sign of SuperSynth's MNI x coordinate at the voxel centre, the rule FreeSurfer splits hemispheres by

runtime_workarounds.conv3d_slices: FreeSurfer 8.2's arm64 torch 2.1.2 has no oneDNN, so CPU conv3d builds a whole-volume im2col buffer (about 90 GB for SuperSynth). scripts/freesurfer/conv3d_slices.py computes the same stride-1 convolution as a sum over kernel depth of 2D convolutions of shifted slices: the same products in a different summation order, matching torch conv3d to 1e-5 relative. Only a convolution whose im2col buffer would reach 1 GiB is sliced; smaller ones run in torch itself, so NextBrain's bias field fit keeps the exact zeros it takes logs of. FireANTs keeps the builtin F.conv3d, which its TorchScript functions bind when they compile.
runtime_workarounds.supersynth_memory_releases: SuperSynth's inference.py drops its first-pass network outputs before the flipped pass, and the flipped outputs once they are averaged in. Only when memory is freed changes.
runtime_workarounds.opencv_stand_in: FreeSurfer 8.2's macOS Python has no OpenCV, yet ERC_bayesian_segmentation's ext/my_functions.py imports cv2 at module level for one helper that asserts False on entry. A stand-in module lets the import succeed and raises if any attribute of it is used.
